items.name: StartError
items.summary: An error that can occur when computing the start state for a search.

items.name: OverlappingState
items.summary: Represents the current state of an overlapping search.

methods.name: get_match
methods.summary: Return the match result of the most recent search to execute with this state.

methods.name: start
methods.summary: Create a new overlapping state that begins at the start state of any automaton.

items.name: Automaton
items.summary: A trait describing the interface of a deterministic finite automaton (DFA).

methods.name: accelerator
methods.summary: Return a slice of bytes to accelerate for the given state, if possible.

methods.name: get_prefilter
methods.summary: Returns the prefilter associated with a DFA, if one exists.

methods.name: has_empty
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this automaton can match the empty string. When it returns false, all possible matches are guaranteed to have a non-zero length.

methods.name: is_accel_state
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given identifier corresponds to an accelerated state.

methods.name: is_always_start_anchored
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if this DFA is limited to returning matches whose start position is `0`.

methods.name: is_dead_state
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given identifier corresponds to a dead state. When a DFA enters a dead state, it is impossible to leave. That is, every transition on a dead state by definition leads back to the same dead state.

methods.name: is_match_state
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given identifier corresponds to a match state. A match state is also referred to as a "final" state and indicates that a match has been found.

methods.name: is_quit_state
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given identifier corresponds to a quit state. A quit state is like a dead state (it has no transitions other than to itself), except it indicates that the DFA failed to complete the search. When this occurs,…

methods.name: is_special_state
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the given identifier corresponds to a "special" state. A special state is one or more of the following: a dead state, a quit state, a match state, a start state or an accelerated state.

methods.name: is_start_state
methods.summary: Returns true only if the given identifier corresponds to a start state

methods.name: is_utf8
methods.summary: Whether UTF-8 mode is enabled for this DFA or not.

methods.name: match_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of patterns that match in this state.

methods.name: match_pattern
methods.signature: fn match_pattern(&self, id: StateID, index: usize) -> PatternID
methods.summary: Returns the pattern ID corresponding to the given match index in the given state.

methods.name: next_eoi_state
methods.summary: Transitions from the current state to the next state for the special EOI symbol.

methods.name: next_state
methods.signature: fn next_state(&self, current: StateID, input: u8) -> StateID
methods.summary: Transitions from the current state to the next state, given the next byte of input.

methods.name: next_state_unchecked
methods.signature: unsafe fn next_state_unchecked(&self, current: StateID, input: u8) -> StateID
methods.summary: Transitions from the current state to the next state, given the next byte of input.

methods.name: pattern_len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of patterns compiled into this DFA.

methods.name: start_state
methods.summary: Return the ID of the start state for this DFA for the given starting configuration.

methods.name: start_state_forward
methods.summary: Return the ID of the start state for this DFA when executing a forward search.

methods.name: start_state_reverse
methods.summary: Return the ID of the start state for this DFA when executing a reverse search.

methods.name: try_search_fwd
methods.summary: Executes a forward search and returns the end position of the leftmost match that is found. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: try_search_overlapping_fwd
methods.signature: fn try_search_overlapping_fwd(&self, input: &Input<'_>, state: &mut OverlappingState) -> Result<(), MatchError>
methods.summary: Executes an overlapping forward search. Matches, if one exists, can be obtained via the [`OverlappingState::get_match`] method.

methods.name: try_search_overlapping_rev
methods.signature: fn try_search_overlapping_rev(&self, input: &Input<'_>, state: &mut OverlappingState) -> Result<(), MatchError>
methods.summary: Executes a reverse overlapping forward search. Matches, if one exists, can be obtained via the [`OverlappingState::get_match`] method.

methods.name: try_search_rev
methods.summary: Executes a reverse search and returns the start of the position of the leftmost match that is found. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: try_which_overlapping_matches
methods.signature: fn try_which_overlapping_matches(&self, input: &Input<'_>, patset: &mut PatternSet) -> Result<(), MatchError>
methods.summary: Writes the set of patterns that match anywhere in the given search configuration to `patset`. If multiple patterns match at the same position and the underlying DFA supports overlapping matches, then all matching patterns are written to th…

methods.name: universal_start_state
methods.summary: If this DFA has a universal starting state for the given anchor mode and the DFA supports universal starting states, then this returns that state's identifier.
